name: fasthands
tagline: Computer use that sends diffs, not screenshots: 91% fewer tokens, any model as the brain
summary: fasthands is an open-source computer-use engine that observes a page once and then sends only what changed. Every click is hash-checked at the moment it fires, so a page that shifts under the agent aborts the batch instead of hitting the wrong button. It runs with Claude, GPT, or a small model on your own laptop.

metrics.label: fewer observation tokens than a screenshot-every-turn loop, over 120 verified runs
metrics.source: README.md: 91.3% fewer tokens and 39.5% fewer turns than the screenshot loop

metrics.label: wrong-button clicks when the page shifts mid-action, against 20 of 20 without the guard
metrics.source: README.md: | fasthands guarded batch | 20 | **0 · 0%** | 20 | **20 · 100%** | and | unguarded batch (fires on stale refs) | 20 | **20 · 100%** | 0 | 0 |

metrics.label: to observe a change on a 2,000-element page, instead of 92,732 to resend the whole tree

features: Observes the page as a compact tree once, then sends diffs with stable element refs
Guarded action batches: every ref is re-hashed before it fires and the batch aborts on drift
xray reads the HTML contract (required, pattern, min/max) and blocks a submit the browser says will fail
Reads canvas draw commands and WebGL scene graphs, and draws with guarded pointer strokes
Works with Anthropic, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama, with no SDK dependencies
how_it_works: The engine takes one compact tree of the interactive page, gives each element a stable ref and content hash, and afterwards sends only diffs.
The model returns a JSON batch of actions; the executor re-hashes every ref before firing and aborts with a drift note if the page changed.
xray adds the page's own validation rules to the observation, so the agent fixes forms before submitting instead of after a failed submit.
install: git clone https://github.com/halleylabs/fasthands && cd fasthands && npm install && npx playwright install chromium
quickstart:
npm run bench -- --repeat 5                               # keyless 120-run headline
node --experimental-strip-types src/bench/drift-test.ts   # 0% vs 100%
node --experimental-strip-types src/bench/scale-test.ts   # scaling curves
node --experimental-strip-types demos/paintbrush.ts <image-url>   # paint anything
